issues.summary: The LinkedIn post sells SSO, RBAC and audit logs on the $6 Business plan, but on the live pricing page those features are in Enterprise at $11.
issues.evidence: assets.linkedin_post.data.post: "If your team needs SSO, RBAC, or audit logs, there's a Business plan at $6/user/month." vs hoppscotch.com/pricing: Enterprise "$11 per user/month, billed annually ... Role-based access controls, SAML-based SSO and OpenID Connect ... Audit logs"

issues.summary: The LinkedIn post opens with an invented first-person migration story that is not in the profile. It also claims request history transfers, which nothing supports. The post was approved with only a warning.
issues.evidence: assets.linkedin_post.data.post: "Migrated from Postman to Hoppscotch in one click. Here's what transferred and what I left behind.\n\nYour collections, environments, and request history come with you."; own warning: "The profile holds no personal migration story."
issues.cause_hint: brand_campaigns hook for the chosen angle ("Migrated from Postman to Hoppscotch in one click. Here's what I kept and what I dropped.") is fed as CAMPAIGN_ANGLE; GLOBAL_RULES line 27 (no tool you used to use) is only a warning, not a blocker, in the LinkedIn gate

issues.summary: The Show HN closing question invents an internal debate about moving Community Edition collaboration features to a paid tier. That is harmful to post for an MIT project and breaks show_hn rule 222.
issues.evidence: assets.show_hn.data.body: "should the Community Edition stay MIT with no feature limits, or should some collaboration features move to a paid self-hosted tier?"
issues.cause_hint: show_hn closer hook ('The choice I want a second opinion on is ...') fills option B freely; no gate enforces rulebooks.ts show_hn 'never an internal debate the profile does not mention'

The MCP server integration (GA) is available on Business and Enterprise cloud tiers." vs docs.hoppscotch.io/documentation/features/ai-features: "The AI bot is available on Enterprise Cloud and Enterprise Self-Host" and MCP "works with both Hoppscotch Cloud and self-hosted instances"

best: The newsletter pitch: one real proof point (80,547 GitHub stars), no competitor named, correct placeholders for editor and builder, true one-liner. Close second: the commercial recommendation mirrors the live $0/$6/$11 pricing accurately.
worst: The LinkedIn post: it opens with a first-person Postman migration story the profile does not hold, and it sells SSO, RBAC and audit logs on the $6 Business plan when they are Enterprise ($11) features. Close second: the Show HN closing question, which invents a debate about moving Community Edition features behind a paywall.
notes: Facts checked live on 2026-09-29: hoppscotch.com/pricing confirms Free $0, Business $6 and Enterprise $11 (per user, billed annually), plus 'MCP server support' in Business. The hoppscotch.com home confirms 'One-Click Migration: Migrate from Postman, Insomnia, cURL with a single click', '5M+ requests every month' and 'Most popular API development tool on GitHub'. The AI features docs say the AI bot is on Enterprise Cloud and Enterprise Self-Host, and the MCP server works on self-hosted instances, which contradicts the 'not available in self-hosted' limitation in four posts and the listing. The main failure pattern is systemic: the chosen angle's competitor-negative and first-person hook, plus the icp.pain wording, flow into LinkedIn, Reddit, Show HN, the reel and a plate brief, and the negative-word gate caught only 'paywalls'. Plan content was judged from 8-plan.png because the plan is not stored in appstate. Postman, Bruno and Insomnia competitor prices were not re-verified.
